title: Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods
summary: Same work, same instrument as dragon-ball-z (Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga, AniList 30042, ch 1-519), so the standing is the same and for the same reason: the film adapts NO chapter — it is an original story set in the gap between two of them. PLACEMENT, FOUR INDEPENDENT SOURCES, ONE SLOT: (1) Toei's press release of 2012-07-17 — 「アニメーションシリーズの「Ｚ」と「ＧＴ」の間、つまり、原作517話で魔人ブウとの戦いが終わった後、518話までの空白の10年の間に起こったエピソードが初めて描かれる」 (same page: 原作 鳥山明 / 監督 細田雅弘 / 脚本 渡辺雄介); (2) ANN 2012-07-14 reporting Weekly Shōnen Jump #33 — 'set between the 517th and 518th installments of Akira Toriyama's original manga… during the "lost decade"'; (3) ja-WP 神と神 概要 — 「原作の第517話と第518話、『ドラゴンボールZ』の第288話と第289話、『ドラゴンボール改』の第157話と第158話の間」, cited to 「DRAGON BALL年代記」『鳥山明 The world of DRAGON BALL パンフレット』東映 2013-03-27 (Age 778, about four years after Buu); (4) dragonball.fandom Timeline placement — 'As a continuation of the manga, its events take place between the manga chapters 517 and 518'. ja-WP is the source that names the slot in Kai's own numbering: 「『ドラゴンボール改』の第157話と第158話の間」. Zero source pages → filler (T27), no chapters (A1); Toriyama's 原作・ストーリー credit is a credit, not an adoption (T26 — and the adoption question on this film is ruled closed, see `adopted`). THE WORK ON THIS SHELF IS THE POSITION, AND IT NEEDS A NUMBERING CONVERSION. The stored 98.5 is the halo's air-date slot (the film opened 2013-03-30, between our row 98 of 2011-08-02 and the Final Chapters' restart on 2014-04-06) and it is a story-order impossibility: row 98 is the END of the Cell arc (ch 419-420), while the film's whole premise is that Majin Buu has been beaten — which this run does not reach until row 164. ja-WP's 157/158 is the JAPANESE numbering; our 167-row space is the INTERNATIONAL one, and the conversion — proved by title and date, not by arithmetic — lands the film at 165.5.

position.why: CORRECTED 98.5 → 165.5 by converting ja-WP's Kai slot (「『ドラゴンボール改』の第157話と第158話の間」) out of the Japanese numbering into ours. (1) OUR SPACE IS THE INTERNATIONAL NUMBERING: 167 rows, while the Fuji TV broadcast of the Buu arc was 61 episodes numbered 99-159 (Kanzenshuu's series index lists Kai as '159 Episodes'). EIGHT of our rows never aired in Japan — 101, 102, 103, 106, 108, 111, 113, 165 (en-WP prints OriginalAirDate '—' with the international-only marker on exactly those eight; batch 19's air-date lane found the same list, research/batch19/out/airdates/dragon-ball-z-kai.json, whose mapping table gives intl 119 = JP 112, intl 128 = JP 121, intl 139 = JP 132). (2) THE SEAM, PROVED BY TITLE + DATE (R20; never by index or by offset arithmetic): ja-WP's JP 157 「やっぱり最強孫悟空!! 魔人ブウ消滅」 (2015-06-14) is en-WP's intl 164 'Son Goku Is the Strongest After All!! Majin Buu Is Annihilated' (same native title, same date); ja-WP's JP 158 「そして10年後…久しぶりの天下一武道会!」 (2015-06-21) is intl 166 'And So, After 10 Years... The First World Martial Arts Tournament in a Long Time!'; JP 159 (2015-06-28) is intl 167. (3) WHAT SITS INSIDE THE SEAM: our row 165 'Peace Returns! A Time of Rest for the Warriors!' is one of the eight international-only episodes — dragonball.fandom's page for it says so ('the eighth out of 8 episodes that had an original title produced for the episode, due to it containing more footage than it's Japanese episode release') and its infobox names the footage it carries: Uncut = 'Celebrations with Majin Buu' + 'He's Always Late', i.e. DBZ eps 287 and 288, the post-Buu peace and the barbecue. That is precisely the material standing between the film and the ten-year jump, so the film goes after it: 165.5. (4) CROSS-CHECK WHERE THE TWO NUMBERINGS MEET: ja-WP's Kai table carries a Z該当話 column — JP 157 = 「286話Aパート中盤-287話」, JP 158 = 「289話-290話Bパート序盤」 (Kai skips DBZ 288, the anime-only party). So the Japanese seam is 'after DBZ 287, before DBZ 289', and this 165.5 and the dragon-ball-z verdict's 288.5 are the same point in the story expressed in two runs' numbering. For the ledger note, in plain words: after Kai's last pre-timeskip episode, before 'And So, Ten Years Later…'. The base row exists (167 rows), so the E2 ledger-base check passes; row 165's own AIR DATE is a separate open item from batch 19 (no Japanese broadcast; AFL's 2018-06-09 is the Toonami premiere) and does not affect this position.

flags_for_sean: TASK PREMISE CORRECTED: the brief calls 98.5 'the base slot (Kai's last episode)'. Our Kai run is 167 rows (ep 167, 2015-06-28, END ch 519); row 98 is only the end of the FIRST Japanese run (the Cell arc, ch 419-420, 2011-08-02) and the Final Chapters are rows 99-167. 98.5 was never 'after the finale' — it is the air-date slot inside the 2011-2014 production gap, sitting before the entire Buu arc the film presupposes.

POSITION: 98.5 → 165.5, derived in position.why. This is the SAME story point as the dragon-ball-z row's proposed 288.5 (ja-WP names both slots in one sentence; ja-WP's Z該当話 column ties them together). Rule them together — if you keep the release-order convention on DBZ (291.5), the Kai analogue is 167.5, not 98.5.

正史 IS NOT A STANDING (same as the DBZ row): Toei 「スピンオフでも番外編でもない、ドラゴンボール正史のストーリー」, 超全集3 「言わば正史である」 — franchise continuity, not chapter coverage. The row stays filler because no page of ch 1-519 is in it.

NO ADOPTION, RULED: THE ADOPTION QUESTION IS ALREADY RULED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Sean, 2026-09-05 (the T26 adoption sitting + batch 22 wave 2, lib/rulings/episode-types.ts T30 pin on DBS ep 6 and lib/rulings/applied/batch-22.ts): 'NO adopted{author} (the bar is 脚本; this film's 脚本 is 渡辺雄介)' — Resurrection 'F' cleared that bar (原作・脚本 鳥山明), Battle of Gods does not. My research CONFIRMS the distinction rather than reopening it: ja-WP draws exactly the same line — 「正確には『神と神』では9割以上の原案・プロットを担当、『復活のF』では初めて脚本を担当した」. So no `adopted` record belongs on any of this film's three rows. Kai's instrument is the same 1995-finished manga, so nothing of the film could have entered it in any case; the film's material lives on in the DRAGON BALL SUPER manga (ch 1-4), recorded there as a shared arc (arcs.ts, A46), not as an adoption.

NUMBERING NOTE WORTH KEEPING: any Japanese source that names a Kai episode number is in the 159-episode broadcast space, not ours. Our 167-row space is Funimation's; the eight rows with no Japanese airing (101, 102, 103, 106, 108, 111, 113, 165) make the offset +7 through the Buu arc and +8 after row 165. Every future Kai join must go through the title, never the number.
